correctness.rationale: Horizontal sections are Minkowski combinations of an aligned cube and crosspolytope. Coordinatewise clipping gives the exact section-volume polynomial through 2^k orthant simplices, and beta integrals give volume and normalized beta-mixture weights rho^k/(k!H_d(rho)). Mixing weights converge in total variation to Pois(rho); fixed-index rescaled Betas converge to Gamma(k+1,1); a finite-mixture truncation then proves the non-Gaussian Poisson–gamma limit. Poisson-majorized beta moments give mean 1+rho and variance 1+2rho. Exact finite rational checks corroborate normalization and moments without purporting to prove infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: This determines the precise high-dimensional localization scale of uniform Euclidean mass in a natural Cayley family joining dual polytopes. Rather than a volume formula alone, it gives an exact all-dimensional probability mixture and identifies a non-Gaussian Bessel-density limit with variable ratio rho and explicit limiting moments. The geometric law is motivated by the extreme contrast in cube and crosspolytope vertex structures, and is a natural structural probability invariant not an arbitrary finite table.
